title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 390 (Offer of Indian Depository Receipts)

content.overview: Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, the Central Government may make rules applicable for— (a) the offer of Indian Depository Receipts; (b) the requirement of disclosures in prospectus or letter of offer issued in connection with Indian Depository Receipts; (c) the manner in which the Indian Depository Receipts shall be dealt with in a depository mode and by custodian and underwriters; and (d) the manner of sale, transfer or transmission of Indian Depository Receipts, by a company incorporated or to be incorporated outside India, whether the company has or has not established, or when formed will or will not establish, a place of business in India.
content.glance: Central Government may make rules for IDR offers, disclosures, depository dealing, and sale/transfer by companies incorporated or to be incorporated outside India.
content.study: Section 390 is an enabling power for Indian Depository Receipts (IDRs). The Central Government may make rules on the offer of IDRs, prospectus or letter-of-offer disclosures, dealing in depository mode by custodians and underwriters, and sale, transfer or transmission of IDRs, by companies incorporated or to be incorporated outside India. An IDR offer is governed by those rules and the applicable SEBI framework; it is not a domestic public issue under Chapter III alone.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: The Central Government may make rules for IDR offers, disclosures, depository dealing, and sale/transfer by foreign (or to-be-incorporated foreign) companies.

examples.title: Illustration — s. 390
examples.body: A company incorporated outside India proposes an IDR issue in India; the offer is governed by rules made under s. 390 and the applicable SEBI IDR framework.

hypotheticals.question: What is the core effect of s. 390?
hypotheticals.analysis: It empowers the Central Government to make rules governing IDR offers by companies incorporated or to be incorporated outside India.

rows.left: Enabling power for Indian Depository Receipts

misconceptions.trap: Treating s. 390 itself as the full substantive code for IDRs.
misconceptions.correction: s. 390 is an enabling rule-making power; the detailed regime is in the rules and the SEBI framework.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should s. 390 be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the IDR offer. II. Apply the rules made under s. 390 and the SEBI framework. III. Do not treat s. 390 alone as a complete code.
